memory_update.text: Keep KLAC as the reference process-control anchor, but do not allow it to crowd out smaller inspection, burn-in, analytics, and packaging-process-control names in later layers.
CAMT is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for HBM, OSAT, chiplet, and advanced-packaging inspection/metrology exposure; verify order durability and customer concentration.
AEHR is a focused but higher-execution-risk test/burn-in candidate tied to AI processor reliability screening; later layers must test whether adoption is broad or customer-specific.
PDFS belongs in the software/data sub-lane of process control: yield analytics, manufacturing data harmonization, test/assembly/packaging analytics, and chiplet complexity.

Later searches should add US-listed or ADR names in probe cards, semiconductor handlers, PCB/substrate inspection, reticle inspection, and back-end metrology, including FORM, COHU, ONTO, NVMI, and possible niche ADRs if evidence supports node purity.

node: Inspection, metrology, yield management, and process-control tools for advanced nodes, HBM, packaging, and PCBs
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around semiconductor process-control intensity created by AI chip complexity. KLA is retained as the reference anchor, but the discovery lane emphasizes smaller or less obvious US-listed assets with inspection, metrology, burn-in, test, and yield-management exposure across advanced packaging, HBM, AI processors, and semiconductor manufacturing analytics. The strongest underfollowed candidates in this pass are Camtek, Aehr Test Systems, and PDF Solutions; all require later validation through customer mix, order durability, segment revenue, and margin sensitivity.
